Production tax credits (PTC) provide a direct financial incentive for new zero-carbon energy projects by reducing their operational costs. Under the Inflation Reduction Act, new zero-carbon resources receive a PTC of $27.50/MWh for the first 10 years of operation, with an additional 10% bonus for projects in energy communities. This credit is applied to variable costs per MWh rather than capital costs, effectively lowering the operating expenses for wind and solar projects during their initial decade of operation. The credit is time-limited (only for the first 10 years), so models must account for this by calculating the present value of the credit (less a 7.5% transfer penalty) and amortizing it over the relevant period. Projects must commence construction by 2036 to qualify for the PTC.
